topics.topic: Whether State 1 authoritatively fixes all OwnerFormField field names and types or delegates them to State 6
questions: Are `name: str`, `carrier: OwnerFormCarrier`, and `reads_as: FormValueKind` authoritative model facts fixed by State 1 and merely carried into State 6, or may State 6 decide their exact names and types?
Replace the candidate heading and the delegation to State 6 with an authoritative State 1 `fields` declaration that fixes every field and its type.
Are these three fields and types definitively fixed by State 1, or are they candidates whose exact declaration may be changed by State 6?

quotes:
Field names, types,
formal optionality and every answer shape belong to State 6; orders, replay
mechanisms, correction semantics and token scopes belong to State 2 (State 0,
"Carried to later states"; codex round-01 T5).

These are all its fields, none optional; their exact names and types are
State 6's, as every field's is (State 0, "Carried to later states"), and
State 6 declares exactly these.
judgement.why: The exact model field names and types are expressly assigned to State 6, while State 1 fixes the domain facts that State 6 must represent, so the candidate wording does not violate §5 at this stage.

topics.topic: How an OwnerFormField row is associated with its owning page, form, or product action
questions: What fact associates an OwnerFormField row with the particular page, form, or product action that displays and reads it?

judgement.why: P1 already judged the same question about associating OWNER_FORM_FIELDS rows with pages or actions, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Association of rows with owner forms or actions and coverage by consuming pages/actions
quotes:
Which action a request names, by its
method and path, and whether it is a change or touches an uploaded file, are
the rows of the data provider's `OWNER_ACTIONS`; its target is the query
parameter `OWNER_TARGET_PARAMETER` names, its CSRF value the form field
`OWNER_CSRF_FIELD` names, every other field it reads or a page writes a row
of `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` (owner, 2026-11-25), the session cookie's name
`OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` and its attributes
`OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES`, and a page's HTTP status the service API's
`SERVICE_ANSWER_STATUS` and `REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES` (owner, 2026-11-24).

Every other field is a row of the
data provider's `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` (`OwnerFormField`). A row's `name` is
the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
(`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
from 0.
precedent.why: The later texts make OWNER_FORM_FIELDS global to every non-target, non-CSRF owner-interface field that a page writes or a request reads, with rows selected by carrier and destination path rather than by a page or action fact.

topics.topic: Where closed-list permitted values are stored and how a list is linked to an OwnerFormField row
questions: When `reads_as` selects a closed list, where are that field's permitted values recorded and how is the particular list associated with this row?

judgement.why: P9 already judged the same question about identifying the closed list and interpreting its selected value, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Identity of the closed list used by a field and the resulting selected value
quotes:
A row's `name` is
the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
(`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
from 0. A row's `reads_as` says how the field's text is read: as the text
itself, an integer's decimal digits, `true` or `false`, or an enumeration
member's value.
precedent.why: The later contract identifies the typed destination by its model path and says a member-valued field produces the destination enumeration's member value, so no separate list identity is left for the generator to guess.

precedent.topic: Whether OwnerFormField is a runtime DTO or structural catalog data
quotes:
The typed constants of the data closure, the one home of each value the
generated code reads that is neither a setting of the environment
(`runtime_settings`) nor a member of an enumeration or a field's type
(`models`) (SPEC_STANDARD
§6.10, §15.3.1; reopened 2026-11-11, replacing the former
release_declarations module):

`models`, for exactly the row models and enumerations of its eight tables:
`ArtifactTypeOwner` (a type with its owner service) and `ServiceName` for
`ARTIFACT_TYPE_OWNERS`; `ServiceRight` (a service and an operation) with
`ServiceName` and `ServiceOperation` for `SERVICE_RIGHTS`;
`ServiceHighestClass` (a service and its highest class) with `ServiceName`
and `DisclosureClass` for `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES`; `PersonalDataField` (an
answer model's name and a field's) for `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS`;
`RefusalHttpStatus` (a code and its status) with `RefusalCode` for
`REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES`; `OwnerActionRoute` (an owner action, its method and
path, whether it is a change and whether it touches an uploaded file) with
`OwnerAction` for `OWNER_ACTIONS`; `OwnerAuditAction` (an owner action,
a customer mark's transition or a project erasure's kind where the action
has one, and the audit action it writes) with `OwnerAction`,
`CustomerTransition`, `ProjectErasure` and `AuditAction` for
`OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS`; `OwnerFormField` (an owner form field's name, the
model it fills and how its text is read) with `OwnerFormCarrier` and
`FormValueKind` for `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`. Its other constants are scalars and import nothing.
precedent.why: State 3 makes OWNER_FORM_FIELDS a typed constant owned by data_provider and makes data_provider depend on the OwnerFormField row model, so the provider constructs and exports OwnerFormField values rather than raw or uninstantiated structural records.
